title: Why he left New Orleans and the Depression
summary: Humphrey gives his reasons for leaving, better pay on the road, and says the Depression kept him away.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: He was related. He's always, everybody always recognized him from, from when he first started to playing, I'll tell you, like, all kind of good old musicians always recognized his playing, you know, see? He would never know Hamlet, like he'd come out playing. Yes. Did he, when he come up? When he first started, he was playing good. Yeah. Of course. When he got acquainted with the musicians, that he played. Yeah. Why did you leave the city? Well, it's about two things. One thing, I wanted to get away from around my wife. I leave town, that was one thing. And, when I was working, it was hard work at the Levita dance hall, with Jenny dancers. And then, I could make a little more money on the road. No expenses, see I did. Oh. The larger paid bus, two meals a day. And, about half more money than I was making on here at this workhouse, Levita dance hall.
And, I had been a traveling man, you know, on different shows anyhow, so, in the spring of the year, coming around, I always feel like moving. Oh. Which I did for a long time.
When you left here, did you, were you, were you meaning to stay away that long? No.

No, I had been going and coming back, about every year, probably every two years. But, this time, out of the way, the depression kind of slipped up, you know. The boys down here wasn't doing anything. And, where I was, that, the first time I went in Jamaica, Georgia, in the winter, 1931, 32. Pickens was pretty good around there. That was a make a living, see.
You were playing fun by that?

Yeah. All I could hear out here, things, closing down, and pressuring, and start to creep up on people, water, no need me coming back here. I could make it, around Macon, Georgia, different places that stopped in the winter times. Oh.
Things that tighten up, you look pretty good. Yes. Were they getting bad before you left? Yeah, it was tight. Yes.
You could tell. I stayed on the road, they, they held up, of course, they cut the sours down.
